facts.text: Appomattox takes its name from the Appomattox River, itself named after the Appomattoc tribe of the Powhatan Confederacy.
The town is home to Appomattox Court House National Historical Park, where General Lee surrendered to Grant in 1865.
During the Civil War, Appomattox Station on the Southside Railroad linked Petersburg and Lynchburg, later becoming part of the Atlantic, Mississippi and Ohio Railroad.
Cub Creek Pottery offers hands‑on pottery workshops, while Steins Unlimited displays thousands of antique German steins in downtown Appomattox.
Visitors can explore the American Civil War Museum, Clover Hill Village, and the Carver‑Price Legacy Museum, all within the historic county.
Each April, the park lights a lantern for every one of the 4,600 slaves freed in Appomattox County during the Civil War.
